item.title: [+1] Sensex rises 473 points to 72,382 as domestic funds absorb ₹4,699 crore of foreign selling
item.description:
The Sensex gained 0.66% and the Nifty 0.6% to 22,555.75, ending a four-session losing streak as crude eased and Fed hike fears faded. Foreign investors sold a net ₹4,699 crore; domestic institutions bought ₹5,182 crore. Relief, but foreign selling continues.

FMCG & consumer: mild tailwind (+1) — Consumer heavyweights led the gains

Why it matters: Domestic funds are cushioning foreign outflows, which limits downside, but persistent foreign selling keeps pressure on index heavyweights and the rupee.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1, Foreign investor flows −2

Confidence: high · horizon: days

item.title: [−1] Brent firms to $100.84 as Gulf and Red Sea attacks keep a risk premium despite better supply
item.description:
Brent rose 0.5% in Asian trade, reversing Monday's dip, as attacks on shipping near Yemen and Hormuz continued; crew pay near the strait has jumped. Brent is up about 3.8% in a month.

FMCG & consumer: mild headwind (−1) — Packaging inputs costlier

Why it matters: Crude near $100 keeps India's import bill, fuel inflation and rupee pressure high, squeezing airlines, fuel marketers and crude-linked manufacturers.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −2, Inflation outlook −1, Rupee −1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks
